title: Students and staff march in Vienna against university funding levels
seoTitle: Vienna student march over university funding

tea.why: Protesters opposed planned university funding levels and cuts in education spending under the government's 2028–2030 budget.
tea.want: Demonstrators demanded that the federal government increase the university budget to close the funding gap and provide adequate resources.
tea.changed: Oct 22: Thousands of students, lecturers, and staff demonstrated in Vienna under the slogan "Red Alert – #SaveTheUniversities!".

summary: Thousands of students, lecturers, and university employees took to the streets of Vienna to protest against planned funding levels for higher education. Organised by the Austrian National Union of Students (ÖH), the demonstration took place under the slogan "Red Alert – #SaveTheUniversities!". Participants marched through central Vienna to oppose a university budget of €16 billion for the years 2028 to 2030, which institutions warn leaves a multibillion-euro shortfall compared to inflation and rising costs. Protesters warned that the budget freeze could lead to reduced educational programs, job cuts, and deteriorating working conditions. The federal government maintained that the allocated amount is final following an agreement by senior officials.
demands: Increase the announced university budget by October 31 to close the funding gap
Ensure sufficient courses and good supervision
Reject additional tuition fees and barriers to access
A fairer distribution of society's wealth
response: The federal government considered the €16 billion funding amount final following an agreement reached by senior officials, according to reports.
